name: King of Bethel
overview: The King of Bethel was a male monarch known primarily as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. His tribal affiliation and personal background are not recorded in Scripture, and no additional notes provide further details about his reign or character. His significance is tied to his role as an opponent overcome by the Israelite leader Joshua.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Bethel' literally means 'king of Bethel,' indicating his rule over the city of Bethel. This designation is a straightforward title rather than a personal name, reflecting his position as the local ruler mentioned in Joshua 12:16.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Bethel beyond his status as a king defeated by Joshua. There are no known relatives or associates mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Bethel is significant in the biblical narrative as one of the regional rulers subdued during Israel's divinely guided conquest of the Promised Land under Joshua's leadership. His defeat symbolizes the fulfillment of God's promise to give the land to Israel and demonstrates the Lord's power in overcoming opposition. Though little is known about him personally, his inclusion among the defeated kings highlights the comprehensive nature of Israel's victory.
